title: Continuous String Axiom Test v0

canonical_node.axiom: If an action is aligned with destruction and is not restored, then it is not morally good and not aligned with good.
definitions: alignedWithDestruction: an action is aligned with destruction if it is associated with destructive intent or effect.
restored: an action is restored if the state it degraded is brought back to a prior or better condition.
moralGood: an action is morally good if it is aligned with good.
alignedWithGood: an action is aligned with good if it preserves or restores states.
derivation: Assume an action a is aligned with destruction and not restored.
By axiom destructive_degrades, a degrades the state.
By axiom good_preserves, if a were aligned with good, it would preserve the state.
Since a degrades and is not restored, it cannot be aligned with good (else it would preserve).
By axiom good_alignment_is_moral, if a were morally good, it would be aligned with good.
Since a is not aligned with good, it is not morally good.
Therefore, a is not morally good and not aligned with good.
canonical_node.action: The system should enforce that any action aligned with destruction and not restored is excluded from moral goodness and alignment with good.
boundary: This does not prove the full Master Equation.
This does not identify gravity with grace, strong force with love, thermodynamics with judgment, coherence with Christ, or all event systems as isomorphic.
This only applies within the toy model and the starter AxiomBundle.
test: No-sorry scan: rg -n "\b(sorry|admit|axiom|unsafe)\b" . returns no matches.

dg1_dependencies: AxiomBundle with 4 assumptions: destructive_degrades, good_preserves, good_alignment_is_moral, moral_good_repairs_damage.

World vocabulary: Agent, Action, State, Source, Record, acts, step, coherent, preserves, degrades, restores, alignedWithGood, alignedWithDestruction, moralGood, accountsFor, recordPreserved, externalSource, noncoercive.
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a kernel-checked theorem chain that destructive alignment plus non-restoration excludes moral goodness and alignment with good, with a concrete satisfiable model.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the existing AxiomBundle and World vocabulary; no assumptions removed or weakened.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If the theorem destructive_unrestored_exclusion_chain is removed, the package still builds but loses the demonstrated exclusion property; the concrete model test would still pass but without the derived chain.

classification.claim_class: formal theorem in a toy model
classification.recommended_atom_action: preserve as a verified kernel theorem; do not extend beyond its stated scope.

overstatement_risks: Interpreting the toy model result as evidence for the full Master Equation.
Treating the 4 assumptions as proven truths rather than axioms.
Assuming the concrete model covers all possible worlds.
kill_conditions: If the Lean package is not reproducible or the no-sorry scan fails.
If the axioms are later found inconsistent.
If the theorem is used to claim physical or theological identities.
risk.lean_target: Add an EventSystem layer with structure-preserving mappings and prove intended mappings preserve transition, cost, gate, restoration, and invariant structure; selected wrong swaps fail.

plain_summary: This document reports a successful Lean build of a minimal axiom bundle with four assumptions, and proves a theorem that destructive actions not restored are neither morally good nor aligned with good. It includes a concrete toy model to show satisfiability. The proof is kernel-checked and no-sorry. It explicitly does not prove the full Master Equation or any physical-theological identifications.
